anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-layer statements or transaction boundaries are written in ways that force the engine to scan or move more data than the business case requires.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database-related processes saturate host CPU, leaving too few cycles for timely request processing.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : The network or connection-handling path between clients and the server becomes a bottleneck, delaying connection establishment or data transfer.

When all three root causes are active, the system exhibits cascading symptoms: inefficient SQL generates excessive logical I/O and large result sets that inflate both CPU demand and outbound payload. The over-consumption of CPU lengthens execution time for every statement, causing run queues, context switches, and scheduler waits to spike. Meanwhile, the same bloated result sets congest network interfaces and exhaust server-side connection resources, producing elevated connection-setup latency, socket backlog growth, and client-side timeouts. Latencies propagate up the stack, leading to stalled application threads, retry storms that further inflate workload volume, and an overall perception of intermittent or widespread outage.

Causally, poor workload logic initiates the spiral by amplifying per-request resource consumption. The swollen CPU usage not only slows query processing but also extends the lifetime of each network transfer, keeping sockets open longer and pushing the listener and kernel queues toward exhaustion. In parallel, delayed network handshakes hold server threads in authentication or client-read waits, preventing them from returning to the pool and increasing CPU pressure on remaining schedulers. The resulting feedback loop—inefficient SQL → CPU saturation → slower execution → prolonged and enlarged network traffic → connection contention—magnifies both resource anomalies and can drive the database into thrashing or partial denial-of-service despite each individual layer appearing only moderately loaded in isolation.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with connection establishment, authentication exchange, protocol correctness, network reachability, or client/server communication stability.
entry.solution_guidance: Check endpoint reachability, authentication flow, connection limits, protocol compatibility, transport stability, and client connection lifecycle management.
